result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers give a usable sorting test and place the log, the camera list and the counting method correctly. They also stick to the supplied facts; the percentages are derived, not invented. B is stronger on the audience. It treats the plant managers as decision-makers by building toward an explicit ask with an owner and a date, and it names the counting method as the likeliest challenge. A only touches on this through an optional action sheet. B's short slide outline stays compact without becoming a full deck. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers give a usable test and sort the audit's material correctly, with the full log, the camera list and the counting method going in the handout. A is more compact and builds the deck around a closing slide that names the decision managers must make, with an owner and a date. B is longer, adds some loosely supported asides, such as calling the 2 to 4 pm finding 'most likely to be cut', and is less explicit about what the managers must approve.
